text:
ben: spun up an experiment: push packing decisions to the edge/router to reduce enqueue jitter. calling it "router-edge packing". main goal: tighten p99 for short-turnaround chats.
maria: Interesting. How do you reconcile that with the scheduler's admission credits and the runtime's continuous-batcher invariants?
ben: Router only aggregates and emits pre-packed batches as a single logical request to runtime. runtime still enforces admission credits and does final slot allocation & KV pinning. router adds a small header with source ids so runtime can map items back to original requests.
kevin: Risk: cross-tenant pack at router could amplify tenant interference. Any fairness guards?
ben: Yep. Router keeps per-tenant soft-credits and a hot-tenant affinity map. If tenant usage > 60% of its soft-credit in a minute, router force-serializes that tenant to single-item fastpath.
sam: What about long sequences? packing short+long together can blow up KV miss rate and tokens/req.
maria: Suggestion: router tags each packed item with `prefix-hint` (sha of first N tokens). runtime uses hint to pre-warm KV asynchronously during enqueue. fallback unchanged for unknown hints.
olga: Could you share the config you're testing?
ben: sure, minimal config we used:```yaml
edge_packing:
  enabled: true
  pack_window_ms: 6
  max_items_per_pack: 12
  min_tokens_to_pack: 8
  tenant_soft_credit_ms: 1000
  hot_tenant_threshold: 0.6
  prefix_hint_length: 32
  kv_prefetch_async: true
  small_request_bypass_tokens: 12
```
natalie: Observability plan: we need new metrics - `edge.pack_rate`, `edge.pack_rejects_hot_tenant`, `edge.prefix_hints_sent`. Also mark traces so we can follow a packed item through runtime: add `X-Pack-Trace-Id`.
kevin: Propose A/B: 15% edge-packing canary vs 85% control. Monitored metrics: p50/p95/p99, runtime.kv_miss_rate, tokens_per_request, eviction_events/sec, and tenant_throughput_skew (95th pctg ratio).
ben: Agree. Fallback rule: if runtime.kv_miss_rate increases by >2.5% absolute within a 10m window, automatically disable edge packing for that shard.
sam: Also add a guard for queueing: router shouldn't mask runtime headroom signals. If runtime returns `queue_headroom_low`, router should delay packing for that shard for 500ms.
olga: Good. We should also avoid making packed groups too heterogeneous. Maybe prefer grouping by model variant and prompt-length bucket.
maria: Implementation note: router will maintain micro-buckets: (model, length_bin) and only coalesce within same bucket unless explicit override. reduces misaligned batches.
natalie: Add eval harness: synthetic mix with 70% short chats (<=20 tokens) and 30% long docs (>=400 tokens) and a hot-tenant at 50% traffic to stress fairness. Collect token/cost regressions and KV miss delta.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary scheduled for infra-canary-12 in 25m. will stream `edge.pack_rate`, `runtime.kv_miss_rate`, and `tenant_throughput_skew`. auto-rollback if p99 increases >10% or kv_miss + tokens/req delta threshold breached.
ben: I'll push the PR w/ config and dashboard links. Action list: Ben = canary + dashboard; Kevin = fairness query + thresholds; Sam = runtime headroom handshake; Olga = micro-bucket heuristics; Maria = eval prompt sets and tracing.
maria: One more ops caution: packed requests make debugging noisy. please ensure we emit original-item-level logs (sparsified) so we can reconstruct spikes.
ben: will include a `edge.unpack-sample` trace that records one-in-N unpacked items per batch.
kevin: Cool. If canary looks stable we can expose as opt-in on dedicated clusters before global rollout.
ben: thanks everyone. I'll post PR link and small runbook for on-call if pack-induced regressions appear.
